vision_features.abnormalities:

The outer stem tissue appears shredded, split, and peeling longitudinally, exposing inner fibrous strands. The surface texture is stringy and frayed, not intact. One central stem shows a medium-sized (approximately 1-2 cm) irregular orange-brown to rust-colored granular mass or deposit adhering to the stem surface at mid-height.

Pod surfaces are crinkled and collapsed inward, suggesting no viable seed fill or that contents have been lost. Pod surfaces are covered in fine pale hairs (consistent with soybean pod pubescence) but appear matted and dusty. Pod edges are ragged and irregular.
3. LEAF REMNANTS: Scattered at the base and along stems are curled, dry, papery leaf fragments that are tan to gray-brown, fully desiccated, and collapsed onto stems and soil. These fragments are irregular in shape and show no green coloration.
4. BASE/SOIL LEVEL: At the base of stems, shredded fibrous plant material is piled on the dark soil surface. Some stem bases appear to have split or fragmented into woody splinters. A whitish-gray fibrous or thread-like coating is visible on some stem bases and fallen plant debris near the soil surface.
vision_features.absences:
1. No green or living tissue is visible on the affected plants in the foreground — all foliage and pod tissue is fully dry and dead.
2. No visible water-soaked or darkened soft-rotted tissue — the affected tissue is dry throughout, not slimy or mushy.
3. No visible powdery white or dusty coating on pod or leaf surfaces beyond the natural fine hair pubescence.
4. No insect bodies, frass, or feeding damage holes are visible on the stems or pods.
vision_features.summary: The foreground plants are severely and uniformly desiccated across all visible organs — stems, pods, and leaf remnants — showing complete loss of green tissue and structural integrity. The stems are particularly striking, with longitudinally shredded, frayed, and split outer tissue exposing inner fibrous strands, and a whitish-gray fibrous matting visible on some stem surfaces. All pods are collapsed, deflated, and uniformly tan-gray with no seed fill apparent. The single most unusual and striking feature is the presence of a small discrete orange-brown granular deposit on one central stem, combined with the overall whitish-gray fibrous coating and shredding of stem tissue throughout the affected area. The stems are the most severely and distinctively affected organ.
